coveragePolicy.reason: Owner has greater personal interest in these regions. Colombia is intentionally more detailed; do not apply its destination count globally.
coveragePolicy.otherRegions: Use a selective representative list with Treasure access and distinct geographic experiences.

latinAmerica.smallerCountries: Use fewer destinations for smaller countries such as Uruguay and Paraguay.
latinAmerica.interpretation: Guideline, not a rigid quota. Prioritize distinct experiences and Treasure access; consolidate nearby places.

rules: Use City (geographic area) as the display label; do not display the term base.
Provide practical overnight destinations for every Treasure; consolidate nearby Treasures when access is reasonable.
Separate accommodation destination from arrival airport; allow multiple airports per destination.
Compare complete flight plus ground-transfer journeys rather than fixing one best airport.
A town may qualify without its own airport when accommodation and attraction access justify staying there.

Consolidate nearby towns and cities that can reasonably be explored during one stay into one representative destination. Different airports, city sizes or amenities alone do not justify separate entries; retain them as linked places and access options.
For one representative island destination, prefer practical airport access; keep distinct archipelagos separate.
Do not infer property-level internet reliability from a city-wide rating.
Add a separate destination when travel practicalities or a distinct geographic area make a separate stay worthwhile; assess journey times rather than using a fixed distance or destination count.

Prioritize coverage of distinctive experiences and landscapes within each country, not just major cities, population or airport size. In South America and Europe, add more destinations when they contribute a genuinely different experience; continue consolidating nearby places that fit into one stay.
